title: CreditSights On China Vanke's Woes, China Bonds Impact
content: Zerlina Zeng, Head of East Asia Corporates and Asia Credit Strategy at CreditSights, sees limited systemic impact and spillover risk to high-grade China dollar bonds from distressed developer China Vanke's request to delay payment on a bond. She speaks with Paul Allen on "Insight with Haslinda Amin." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fitch Pushes Colombia Further Into Junk Citing Fiscal Deficits
content: Fitch Ratings downgraded Colombia’s credit rating one notch deeper into junk territory, citing persistently large budget deficits that will add to the nation’s debt load.

title: Singapore Bank UOB Struggles With Hong Kong, China Property Loans as Prices Sink
content: A large wager on Hong Kong and China real estate is backfiring on one of Singapore’s top banks, which is facing up to mounting troubles in the region’s deteriorating property markets.

title: KIK Custom Gets Rescue Loan From New Lenders Including Oaktree
content: KIK Custom Products Inc. received a $150 million rescue loan from new lenders, including Oaktree Capital Management to help the cleaning-products company bridge a potential liquidity shortfall, according to people familiar with the situation.

title: Sluggish Jobs Report Hints at Cooling Labor Market | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 12/16/2025
content: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss US job growth remaining sluggish in November and the unemployment rate rising to a four year high, all pointing to a cooling US labor market. Bloomberg's Michael McKee joins the show to break it down. Plus, Whalen Global Advisors Chairman Chris Whalen joins to discuss market risks, private credit, tech investments, and more. Also on today's show, MARA CEO Fred Thiel discusses how bitcoin fatigue is setting in as the token heads for its fourth yearly decline, and US Department of Labor Chief Economist Julia Pollak on today's payrolls data. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How Chinese Brands Are Going Global
content: From Pop Mart’s Labubus to Shein, Temu and Luckin, Chinese brands have become global consumer favorites and cultural ambassadors. With much of the credit going to TikTok, shoppers are hungry for more. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Seed Funding In 2025 Broke Records Around Big Rounds And AI, With US Far In The Lead
content: The seed investment environment exhibited its typical quirkiness in 2025. In particular, it was a huge year for huge rounds. Predictably, it was also a banner period for AI dealmaking with the U.S. pulling in a bigger-than-usual share of total investment.

content: Democrats in the House back a last-ditch effort to extend Obamacare subsidies, which relies on a tactic recently used for the Jeffrey Epstein files bill.

title: Trump officials move slowly on student loan forgiveness, repayment plan backlog: court filing
content: Hundreds of thousands of student loan borrowers remain stuck in a backlog of requests for an affordable payment plan or debt forgiveness, a court filing shows.

title: Esusu, platform for renters to build credit scores, valued at $1.2 billion in new funding round

title: What another Fed cut could mean for your personal borrowing costs
content: Many types of consumer loans are impacted when the Fed lowers its overnight lending rate, but it also depends on the product and duration.

title: Mortgage rates hit highest level in a month, pushing loan demand down 5%
content: Mortgage rates rose to the highest level in a month last week, causing demand for home loans to drop. Demand, however, is still higher than a year ago.
